html:
The Yekooche are a small First Nation of the Dakelh, or Carrier, people of central British Columbia, living at the north end of Stuart Lake. Their village sits on the old portage between Stuart Lake and Babine Lake, so in English it was long called Portage.

The Dakelh speak an Athabaskan language and lived from salmon runs, hunting and trapping. In 1806 Simon Fraser of the North West Company built a post at Fort St. James on Stuart Lake, which became the centre of the fur trade of New Caledonia. Today about 250 people belong to the Yekooche Nation. Their neighbours include the Nadleh Whut'en to the south.
